cardTitle: Genomic Profiling for Cancer Subtype Identification
cardAbstract: This project focuses on using genomic data to classify cancer subtypes, providing insights into personalized treatment approaches. Researchers in this project employ advanced genomic profiling techniques to categorize different cancer subtypes more accurately. By understanding the genomic basis of each subtype, the project aims to personalize cancer treatment strategies for better outcomes.
dataSharing: De-identified data shared with scientific community

cardAbstract: Immunotherapy Advancements is dedicated to exploring novel approaches for enhancing the effectiveness of immunotherapy in treating cancer. The project focuses on developing innovative immunotherapy techniques, including checkpoint inhibitors and CAR-T cell therapies. Researchers aim to make immunotherapy more effective and accessible to a broader range of cancer patients.
dataSharing: De-identified data shared with the scientific community

cardAbstract: Epidemiological Studies analyze cancer incidence data to understand the factors contributing to cancer prevalence and potential preventive measures. This project examines the demographic and environmental factors associated with varying cancer incidence rates. By identifying these factors, researchers hope to develop preventive measures and public health strategies to reduce the incidence of specific cancer types.
dataSharing: Aggregated data shared with the scientific community

cardAbstract: Metabolomics Research investigates the metabolic pathways in cancer cells, offering potential targets for cancer therapies. Researchers study the metabolic processes within cancer cells to discover vulnerabilities that can be targeted with new therapies. This project aims to develop drugs and treatment strategies that disrupt cancer cell metabolism, hindering their growth and progression.
dataSharing: De-identified data shared with the scientific community

cardAbstract: Machine Learning for Cancer Diagnosis project develops AI models for early cancer detection, improving diagnostic accuracy. The project uses machine learning algorithms to analyze medical imaging and patient data for early detection of various cancer types. The goal is to reduce false negatives and positives, leading to more accurate diagnoses and improved patient outcomes.
dataSharing: De-identified data shared with the scientific community
contactInformation: Machine Learning Department, Cancer Diagnosis Institute

cardAbstract: This project focuses on educating the public about immunology and the benefits of immunotherapy in cancer treatment. The project conducts outreach programs, workshops, and public awareness campaigns to inform individuals about the role of the immune system in fighting cancer. By promoting immunology education, the project seeks to empower patients and improve their understanding of immunotherapy options.

cardTitle: Cancer Clinical Trials and Drug Development
cardAbstract: Cancer Clinical Trials and Drug Development seeks to design and conduct clinical trials for promising cancer drugs. This project collaborates with pharmaceutical companies, medical institutions, and regulatory authorities to establish and oversee clinical trials. By providing a structured approach to drug testing, the project aims to accelerate the development of new cancer treatments.

Functional Genomics in Cancer Research project investigates how specific genes and genetic variations contribute to cancer development. Researchers aim to understand the functional consequences of genetic mutations and their role in cancer progression. The insights gained may lead to the identification of novel therapeutic targets and treatment approaches.

cardTitle: Cancer Incidence Trends in Urban Environments
cardAbstract: Cancer Incidence Trends in Urban Environments project analyzes the changing patterns of cancer incidence in urban areas. Researchers examine lifestyle factors and environmental conditions contributing to the rise or decline of specific cancer types. The findings may inform urban planning and public health initiatives.

cardTitle: Genetic Biomarkers for Early Cancer Detection
cardAbstract: Genetic Biomarkers for Early Cancer Detection project focuses on identifying genetic biomarkers associated with different cancer types. Researchers aim to develop non-invasive tests for early cancer detection by analyzing genetic variations in blood or other samples. Early detection can lead to more effective treatments and improved survival rates.

Immunotherapy in Solid Tumor Treatment project concentrates on enhancing immunotherapy techniques for solid tumor cancers. Researchers investigate the unique challenges presented by solid tumors and explore immunotherapeutic strategies to target these cancers effectively. The project aims to improve outcomes for patients with solid tumor malignancies.

cardTitle: Cancer Risk Factors in Aging Populations
cardAbstract: Cancer Risk Factors in Aging Populations project examines the specific risk factors contributing to cancer in older individuals. Researchers analyze lifestyle, genetics, and other factors to better understand the increased cancer risk in aging populations. The findings may lead to tailored prevention and screening programs.

Functional Genomics in Leukemia Research project focuses on the functional genomics of leukemia, aiming to discover new treatment options. Researchers investigate the genetic basis of different leukemia subtypes, seeking to identify therapeutic vulnerabilities. The project may lead to the development of targeted therapies for leukemia patients.

Immunotherapy and Checkpoint Inhibitors project delves into the use of checkpoint inhibitors in cancer immunotherapy. Researchers focus on optimizing checkpoint inhibitor therapies to enhance their effectiveness in various cancer types. The project aims to broaden the applications of immunotherapy and improve patient responses.
